newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shareholder group seek info on bank rumour.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shareholder group seek info on bank rumour.

text.p: Swedish private shareholders' pressure group, Aktiespararna, is to seek clarification from S-E-Banken and Handelsbanken after business daily Dagens Industri (DI) at the weekend reported the two Swedish banks were in tentative merger talks, DI said on Monday.
Aktiespararna's chief lawyer, Lars Milberg, said the fact that neither bank had commented on the article was unacceptable.
"The banks ought to explain the situation to the Stockholm Stock Exchange -- if not, trade in both banks should be suspended ahead of an explanation," Milberg told the newspaper.
"In this extremely sensitive situation they should either make a quick denial or provide information on the situation or when the information will be given."
Lars Bredin, vice president of the Stockholm Stock exchange, said the bourse had not received any information from either bank.
"I cannot rule out the possibility that I will contact the banks on Monday morning," Bredin told Dagens Industri.

On Saturday, Dagens Industri reported that the banks, two of the top four in Sweden, had started tentative merger talks to establish a strong base in Sweden's competitive banking sector ahead of Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999.
It said the heads of the two banks had met several times in recent weeks.
Dagens Industri said any decision to proceed was expected to be made during the first half of next year at the latest.
